refuted_blocking.claim_broken: restore.md A6 (infra/runbooks/restore.md:113) says schema ACLs must be identical, and R92 says a real ACL difference is still named after normalisation. But no test fails when the schemas family stops reading nspacl at all. bk01g only proves the equal direction for a schema (NULL vs the owner default spelled out). Its only real-loss assertion (the '{}' revoke) is on a table, and bk01f's DAMAGE has no schemas entry.
refuted_blocking.evidence: Mutant M5 (pgrestore.py:274), one edit: `unnest(coalesce(nspacl, acldefault('n', ` -> `unnest(coalesce(null, acldefault('n', `. The schemas family then compares only the owner's default and is blind to every schema grant. Whole test_restore.py on d3/Supabase with this mutant: exit 0, `21 passed, 3 deselected` (the 3 are E2-only). SURVIVED. On pristine code the attack `grant usage on schema infrx to anon` against a good restore gives exactly ["schemas differ: ... extra [('infrx', '{anon=U/postgres,postgres=UC/postgres,service_role=U/postgres}')]"]. So the check works today, but nothing pins it. Keeping infrx hidden from anon is a tenant-boundary property (0008). This gap predates R92, but R92 edited this same expression and tested only its equal direction.
refuted_blocking.minimal_fix: Add one bk01f DAMAGE entry, `"schemas": "grant usage on schema infrx to anon"` (measured: compare names exactly {schemas}). Add a mutant in mutants_i3b.py with M5's edit, named bk01f and schemas.

nonblocking.claim_broken: The lane says 'the fixture does not allow the plain image'. That is true in effect, but INFRX_I3B_PG=d with no INFRX_D1_IMAGE is not refused. The fixture carries plain-image code paths (lines 133 and 150: the _admin superuser branch and the NEEDS_SHIM shim apply), and they cannot work for 13 of the 24 cases. The failure is loud, but the configuration looks supported when it is not.
nonblocking.evidence: Reproduced exactly on d3 with the plain image: `5 failed, 10 passed, 1 skipped, 8 errors`. Every restore-dependent case (bk01_a/b/c/h, bk01f x8 via good_restore) stops at `pg_restore failed (1): ... unrecognized configuration parameter "transaction_timeout" / Command was: SET transaction_timeout = 0;`. The client that fails is the throwaway `infrx-i3b-pgclient-*` container from pgrestore.IMAGE: `pg_restore (PostgreSQL) 17.6`. The plain server is `postgres (PostgreSQL) 16.14`. The host's own pg_restore (16.15) is never used. So the lane's diagnosis is correct: a 17 client into a 16 server. bk02 fails at `psycopg.errors.UndefinedColumn: column "confirmed_at" of relation "users" does not exist`. HOSTED_SEED inserts into hosted/Supabase's auth.users.confirmed_at, and D's shim (supabase_shim.sql:58) has only email_confirmed_at. That is a shim schema difference, not a fixture bug.
nonblocking.minimal_fix: In needs_pg(), when ON_D and not d_harness().ON_SUPABASE, call pytest.fail('INFRX_I3B_PG=d needs INFRX_D1_IMAGE=supabase: pgrestore.IMAGE is a 17.6 client (transaction_timeout) and the shim has no auth.users.confirmed_at'). Delete the dead plain branches at lines 133 and 150. Use fail, not skip, so a plain run cannot go green without testing anything.

nonblocking.claim_broken: R92 says the check compares ACLs by the privileges they grant. Column privileges (pg_attribute.attacl) are in no family, and the project uses one: 0001_init.sql:208 `grant update (full_name, avatar_url) on public.profiles to authenticated`. This predates the lane and is not caused by the coalesce normalisation.
nonblocking.evidence: Against a good d3/Supabase restore, `revoke update (full_name) on public.profiles from authenticated` gives pg.compare == []. So does `grant update (full_name) on public.profiles to anon`, which is a widening. Both measured.
nonblocking.minimal_fix: Add a family: `select attrelid::regclass::text, attname, array(select unnest(attacl)::text order by 1)::text from pg_attribute where attrelid in (select c.oid from pg_class c join pg_namespace n on n.oid=c.relnamespace where n.nspname = any(%(s)s)) and attnum > 0 and not attisdropped and attacl is not null order by 1,2`. attacl has no owner default, so NULL needs no normalisation. Add a bk01f DAMAGE entry using the revoke above.

nonblocking.claim_broken: The lens asked whether an owner change hides an ACL change. It does not: acldefault takes the owner, and ALTER OWNER rewrites explicit ACLs. The one blind spot is an object whose ACL is '{}' (revoked from its owner): an owner change there leaves the fingerprint unchanged, because no family compares owners.

The pre-R92 catalog would have missed that on any NULL-ACL object. `alter function infrx.put_result(jsonb) owner to supabase_admin` is named (functions, grantor rewritten).
